def _check_chain_merge_memory():
    # Merging a source chain onto a target keeps the target's old
    # segments, appends exactly one target-owned delta and makes the
    # target load to the source's merge-time state bit for bit; the
    # source chain (head and files) is never modified and the two chains
    # keep evolving independently.
    seq, _ = _fresh_stack()
    source = _checkpoint.MemoryChain()
    seq.save(source)  # seg 0
    out, _ = seq.forward(Tensor(_SEG1))
    seq.backward(_total(out))
    seq.update(_LR)
    seq.save(source)  # seg 1 (hidden introduced)
    seq.adam_step(_ADAM_LR)
    seq.save(source)  # seg 2 (optimizer state moves)

    # The target forks at seg 1 and then diverges on its own.
    target = _checkpoint.fork_chain_memory(source, up_to=1)
    branch_seq, _ = _fresh_stack()
    branch_hidden = branch_seq.load(target)
    out2, branch_hidden = branch_seq.forward(Tensor(_SEG2), branch_hidden)
    branch_seq.backward(_total(out2))
    branch_seq.adam_step(_ADAM_LR)
    branch_seq.save(target)  # target seg 2 differs from source seg 2

    source_state = _checkpoint.build_bytes(
        _checkpoint.load_chain_memory(source)
    )
    source_head_before = source.read_head()
    target_head_before = int(target.read_head())
    segments_before = len(target)

    _checkpoint.merge_chains_memory(source, target)

    _check(
        target.read_head() == str(target_head_before + 1).encode("ascii"),
        "a merge advances the target head by exactly one",
    )
    _check(
        len(target) == segments_before + 1,
        "a merge appends exactly one segment",
    )
    _check(
        source.read_head() == source_head_before,
        "a merge never moves the source head",
    )
    _check(
        _checkpoint.build_bytes(_checkpoint.load_chain_memory(target))
        == source_state,
        "the merged target loads to the source's merge-time state bit for bit",
    )
    _check(
        _checkpoint.build_bytes(_checkpoint.load_chain_memory(source))
        == source_state,
        "a merge leaves the source chain state untouched",
    )
    source_doc = _checkpoint.load_chain_memory(source)
    target_doc = _checkpoint.load_chain_memory(target)
    _check(
        target_doc["optim"]["t"] == source_doc["optim"]["t"],
        "a merge inherits the step count rather than advancing it",
    )

    # A full save after the merge lands exactly the merged state.
    merged_seq, _ = _fresh_stack()
    merged_seq.load(target)
    full = bytearray()
    merged_seq.save(full)
    _check(
        bytes(full) == source_state,
        "a full save after a merge lands exactly the merged state",
    )

    # Re-merging the same state appends an empty delta and changes the
    # state not at all; the segment count still grows with the call.
    _checkpoint.merge_chains_memory(source, target)
    empty_index = target_head_before + 2
    _n, _hc, _p, empty_items = _checkpoint._parse_delta(
        target.read_segment(_checkpoint._segment_name(empty_index)), empty_index
    )
    _check(empty_items == [], "re-merging an equal state appends an empty delta")
    _check(
        _checkpoint.build_bytes(_checkpoint.load_chain_memory(target))
        == source_state,
        "an empty merge delta keeps the state exactly the same",
    )

    # Both chains then evolve independently; the merge target never
    # shares state by mutation with the source.
    source_seq, _ = _fresh_stack()
    source_seq.load(source)
    source_seq.update(_LR)
    source_seq.save(source)
    target_seq, _ = _fresh_stack()
    target_seq.load(target)
    target_seq.update(_LR)
    target_seq.save(target)
    _check(
        _checkpoint.build_bytes(_checkpoint.load_chain_memory(source))
        == _checkpoint.build_bytes(_checkpoint.load_chain_memory(target)),
        "identical post-merge steps keep the chains in lockstep",
    )
    target_seq.adam_step(_ADAM_LR)
    target_seq.save(target)
    _check(
        _checkpoint.build_bytes(_checkpoint.load_chain_memory(source))
        != _checkpoint.build_bytes(_checkpoint.load_chain_memory(target)),
        "a later change on one chain leaves the other independent",
    )
    _check(
        _checkpoint.verify_chain_memory(source).ok
        and _checkpoint.verify_chain_memory(target).ok,
        "both chains verify after a merge and independent evolution",
    )

    # Merging a fork point straight across needs no change at all: the
    # appended delta is empty even when the target had a different tail.
    ancestor = _checkpoint.MemoryChain()
    base_seq, _ = _fresh_stack()
    base_seq.save(ancestor)
    out, hidden = base_seq.forward(Tensor(_SEG1))
    base_seq.backward(_total(out))
    base_seq.update(_LR)
    base_seq.save(ancestor)  # seg 1
    twin = _checkpoint.fork_chain_memory(ancestor, up_to=1)
    _checkpoint.merge_chains_memory(ancestor, twin)
    _n, _hc, _p, items = _checkpoint._parse_delta(
        twin.read_segment(_checkpoint._segment_name(2)), 2
    )
    _check(items == [], "merging an equal head state appends an empty delta")

    # Error taxonomy.
    _expect(
        ValueError,
        lambda: _checkpoint.merge_chains_memory(source, source),
        "merging a chain into itself is rejected",
    )
    empty = _checkpoint.MemoryChain()
    _expect(
        ValueError,
        lambda: _checkpoint.merge_chains_memory(source, empty),
        "merging onto a chain with no committed basis is rejected",
    )
    _expect(
        ValueError,
        lambda: _checkpoint.merge_chains_memory(empty, target),
        "merging from a chain with no committed basis is rejected",
    )
    _expect(
        TypeError,
        lambda: _checkpoint.merge_chains_memory(object(), target),
        "merge rejects a non-MemoryChain source",
    )
    _expect(
        TypeError,
        lambda: _checkpoint.merge_chains_memory(source, object()),
        "merge rejects a non-MemoryChain target",
    )

    # Two chains whose parameter shapes disagree are rejected wholesale
    # and leave the target byte for byte untouched.
    other_weights = _base_weights()
    other_weights["b1"] = [0.01, -0.02]  # shape [2] instead of [3]
    shaped_seq, _ = _fresh_stack(other_weights)
    shaped = _checkpoint.MemoryChain()
    shaped_seq.save(shaped)
    target_bytes_before = sorted(
        (name, target.read_segment(name))
        for name in target._objects
        if _checkpoint._segment_index(name) is not None
    )
    target_head_saved = target.read_head()
    _expect(
        ValueError,
        lambda: _checkpoint.merge_chains_memory(shaped, target),
        "chains with mismatched parameter shapes refuse a merge",
    )
    _check(
        target.read_head() == target_head_saved
        and sorted(
            (name, target.read_segment(name))
            for name in target._objects
            if _checkpoint._segment_index(name) is not None
        )
        == target_bytes_before,
        "a rejected merge leaves the target untouched",
    )

    # A missing referenced segment in the source is a FileNotFoundError
    # (a directory or a referenced segment that is absent) and leaves
    # the target untouched.
    hole = _checkpoint.fork_chain_memory(source)
    del hole._objects[_checkpoint._segment_name(1)]
    head_saved = target.read_head()
    _expect(
        FileNotFoundError,
        lambda: _checkpoint.merge_chains_memory(hole, target),
        "a source missing a referenced segment raises FileNotFoundError",
    )
    _check(target.read_head() == head_saved, "target unchanged after a bad source")

    # The container-level entry point merges memory chains too.
    via_seq, _ = _fresh_stack()
    c1 = _checkpoint.MemoryChain()
    via_seq.save(c1)
    via_seq.update(_LR)
    via_seq.save(c1)
    c2 = _checkpoint.fork_chain_memory(c1, up_to=0)
    via_seq.merge(c1, c2)
    _check(
        _checkpoint.build_bytes(_checkpoint.load_chain_memory(c2))
        == _checkpoint.build_bytes(_checkpoint.load_chain_memory(c1)),
        "Sequential.merge merges two memory chains",
    )
    _expect(
        TypeError,
        lambda: via_seq.merge(c1, bytearray()),
        "merge rejects mismatched target kinds",
    )
    _expect(
        TypeError,
        lambda: via_seq.merge(bytearray(), c2),
        "merge rejects mismatched source kinds",
    )


def _check_streaming_compaction_interleaves():
    # The streaming fold keeps working through concurrent appends and
    # reads: a compactor, an appender and readers run at once against one
    # in-memory chain and every observed state is a complete, loadable
    # chain.  The final chain compacts to one basis matching its head.
    seq, _ = _fresh_stack()
    chain = _checkpoint.MemoryChain()
    seq.save(chain)
    errors = []
    stop = False

    def appender():
        try:
            for _ in range(120):
                doc = _checkpoint.load_chain_memory(chain)
                _checkpoint.save_chain_memory(doc, chain)  # empty delta
        except BaseException as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
            errors.append(exc)

    def reader():
        try:
            while not stop:
                _checkpoint.build_bytes(_checkpoint.load_chain_memory(chain))
        except BaseException as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
            errors.append(exc)

    threads = [threading.Thread(target=appender)]
    threads += [threading.Thread(target=reader) for _ in range(2)]
    for thread in threads:
        thread.start()
    for _ in range(30):
        _checkpoint.compact_chain_memory(chain)
    stop = True
    for thread in threads:
        thread.join()
    _check(errors == [], f"streaming interleave raised: {errors!r}")
    head_bytes = _checkpoint.build_bytes(_checkpoint.load_chain_memory(chain))
    _checkpoint.compact_chain_memory(chain)
    _check(len(chain) == 1, "the interleaved chain finally folds to one basis")
    _check(
        _checkpoint.build_bytes(_checkpoint.load_chain_memory(chain)) == head_bytes,
        "the folded chain preserves the head state bit for bit",
    )


def _check_chain_verification():
    # A sound chain verifies and reports the head/segment count.
    seq, _ = _fresh_stack()
    chain = _checkpoint.MemoryChain()
    seq.save(chain)
    out, _ = seq.forward(Tensor(_SEG1))
    seq.backward(_total(out))
    seq.save(chain)
    seq.update(_LR)
    seq.save(chain)
    report = _checkpoint.verify_chain_memory(chain)
    _check(report.ok and report.head == 2 and report.segments == 3,
           "a sound chain verifies with a success report")
    probe, _ = _fresh_stack()
    _check(probe.verify(chain).ok, "Sequential.verify reads a sound chain")

    # A truncated delta is rejected at that segment, naming position/reason.
    seg1 = chain.read_segment(_checkpoint._segment_name(1))
    chain.write_segment(_checkpoint._segment_name(1), seg1[: len(seg1) // 2])
    try:
        _checkpoint.verify_chain_memory(chain)
    except ValueError as exc:
        message = str(exc)
        _check("segment 1" in message, f"verify names the first bad segment: {message}")
    else:
        raise _SelfTestFailure("a truncated segment must fail verification")
    chain.write_segment(_checkpoint._segment_name(1), seg1)
    _check(_checkpoint.verify_chain_memory(chain).ok,
           "the chain verifies once the segment is whole")

    # A truncated basis is located at segment 0.
    seg0 = chain.read_segment(_checkpoint._segment_name(0))
    chain.write_segment(_checkpoint._segment_name(0), seg0[:20])
    try:
        _checkpoint.verify_chain_memory(chain)
    except ValueError as exc:
        _check("segment 0" in str(exc), "a bad basis is located at segment 0")
    else:
        raise _SelfTestFailure("a truncated basis must fail verification")
    chain.write_segment(_checkpoint._segment_name(0), seg0)

    # A corrupt head pointer is rejected (not mistaken for an empty chain).
    chain.write_head(b"not-a-number")
    _expect(ValueError, lambda: _checkpoint.verify_chain_memory(chain),
            "a corrupt head pointer fails verification")
    chain.write_head(b"2")

    # An empty chain (no head) is rejected wholesale.
    _expect(
        ValueError,
        lambda: _checkpoint.verify_chain_memory(_checkpoint.MemoryChain()),
        "an empty chain fails verification",
    )
    _expect(TypeError, lambda: _checkpoint.verify_chain_memory(object()),
            "verify rejects a non-MemoryChain")


class _BoomBackwardAndReplayRNN(_RNNStep):
    """Layer whose first backward raises and whose cache-rebuild replay
    also raises, so the rebuild failure must be surfaced, not swallowed."""

    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
        self._boom = True
        self._fail_replay = False

    def forward(self, x, hidden):
        if self._fail_replay:
            raise ValueError("replay forward failed")
        return super().forward(x, hidden)

    def backward(self, upstream):
        if self._boom:
            self._boom = False
            self._cache = None
            raise RuntimeError("layer backward failed")
        return super().backward(upstream)

            errors.append(exc)

    def probe_state(model):
        _check(model._adam_t >= 0, "a loaded checkpoint carries a valid step count")
        for param, m, v in zip(
            model.parameters(), model._adam_m, model._adam_v
        ):
            for tree in (param.tolist(), m, v, param.grad.tolist()):
                for value in _flatten(tree):
                    _check(
                        isinstance(value, (int, float))
                        and value == value
                        and value not in (float("inf"), float("-inf")),
                        "a concurrently saved checkpoint is fully finite",
                    )

    def buffer_roundtrip():
        try:
            for _ in range(200):
                buf = bytearray()
                seq.save(buf)
                probe, _ = _fresh_stack()
                probe.load(bytes(buf))
                probe_state(probe)
        except BaseException as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
            errors.append(exc)

    def chain_roundtrip():
        chain = _checkpoint.MemoryChain()
        try:
            for _ in range(200):
                seq.save(chain)
                probe, _ = _fresh_stack()
                probe.load(chain)
                probe_state(probe)
        except BaseException as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
            errors.append(exc)

    def loader_to_base():
        try:
            for _ in range(200):
                seq.load(bytes(base))
        except BaseException as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
            errors.append(exc)

    threads = (
        [threading.Thread(target=stepper) for _ in range(3)]
        + [
            threading.Thread(target=buffer_roundtrip),
            threading.Thread(target=chain_roundtrip),
            threading.Thread(target=loader_to_base),
        ]
    )
    for thread in threads:
        thread.start()
    for thread in threads:
        thread.join()
    _check(errors == [], f"concurrent adam run raised: {errors!r}")

"""Tests for chain forks: branch chains sharing a prefix segment family.

A chain forked at segment *k* produces a second chain directory whose
segments ``0..k`` are hard links to the source chain's files, plus its
own ``head``; from then on each chain maintains only its own head and
appended deltas.  These tests cover:

* prefix sharing and head independence (the shared files are stored
  once; appends to the same segment position never interfere);
* bitwise equivalence with chains that never forked, through saves,
  loads, streaming compactions and branch deletion on both sides;
* deterministic, reachability-based reclamation of shared segments;
* the fork error taxonomy (ValueError / FileNotFoundError / OSError)
  and kill-at-any-point safety of the fork itself;
* read-only verification of a whole chain family, reporting the first
  bad segment together with the chain it belongs to.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import errno
import hashlib
import json
import multiprocessing
import os
import shutil
import struct
import tempfile
import threading
import time
import unittest
import zlib
from unittest import mock

from sequence_engine import MemoryChain, Sequential, Tensor
from sequence_engine import checkpoint as cp
from sequence_engine._selftest import (
    _base_weights,
    _build,
    _SEG1,
    _SEG2,
    _total,
)

_LR = 0.1
_ADAM_LR = 0.05


def _stack(weights=None):
    return _build(weights if weights is not None else _base_weights())


def _seg(i):
    return f"seg-{i:010d}.seqd"


def _train(seq, td, steps, hidden=None, start=0):
    """Run *steps* deterministic train/save cycles numbered from *start*."""
    for i in range(start, start + steps):
        out, hidden = seq.forward(Tensor(_SEG1 if i % 2 == 0 else _SEG2), hidden)
        seq.backward(_total(out))
        if i % 3 == 2:
            seq.adam_step(_ADAM_LR)
        else:
            seq.update(_LR)
        seq.save(td)
    return hidden


def _trained_dir(td, steps):
    """A fresh chain directory: basis save + *steps* cycles (head == steps)."""
    os.mkdir(td)
    seq, _ = _stack()
    seq.save(td)
    hidden = _train(seq, td, steps)
    return seq, hidden


def _chain_state(td):
    return cp.build_bytes(cp.load_chain(td))


def _dir_hash(td):
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    for name in sorted(os.listdir(td)):
        path = os.path.join(td, name)
        if os.path.isfile(path):
            digest.update(name.encode("ascii"))
            with open(path, "rb") as fh:
                digest.update(fh.read())
    return digest.hexdigest()


def _read(path):
    with open(path, "rb") as fh:
        return fh.read()


def _renumber_delta(path, new_number):
    raw = _read(path)
    hlen = struct.unpack("<Q", raw[12:20])[0]
    header = json.loads(raw[20 : 20 + hlen])
    payload = raw[20 + hlen : raw.rfind(cp.DELTA_END_MAGIC)]
    header["n"] = new_number
    new_header = json.dumps(
        header, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True
    ).encode("utf-8")
    body = (
        raw[:8]
        + struct.pack("<I", cp.FORMAT_VERSION)
        + struct.pack("<Q", len(new_header))
        + new_header
        + payload
    )
    crc = zlib.crc32(body[20:])
    return body + cp.DELTA_END_MAGIC + struct.pack("<QI", len(payload) // 9, crc)


def _reshape_first_delta_entry(path, shape):
    raw = _read(path)

"""Tests for the streaming online compaction, read-only chain
verification and the surfaced backward cache-rebuild failure.

These complement the black-box compaction/recovery tests in
``test_v4_compact.py`` by exercising the new guarantees directly:

* compaction streams: saves and loads interleave and the on-disk peak
  stays within the original chain plus one new basis segment;
* ``verify_chain`` / ``Sequential.verify`` locate the first bad segment
  and never write a byte;
* a backward whose cache-rebuild replay also fails surfaces that failure
  as a ``ValueError`` chained onto the original layer exception.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import os
import struct
import tempfile
import threading
import zlib
import unittest

from sequence_engine import MemoryChain, Sequential, Tensor
from sequence_engine import checkpoint as cp
from sequence_engine._selftest import (
    _base_weights,
    _build,
    _RNNStep,
    _SEG1,
    _total,
)

_LR = 0.1


def _stack(weights=None):
    return _build(weights if weights is not None else _base_weights())


def _seg(i):
    return f"seg-{i:010d}.seqd"


def _trained_dir(td, steps):
    seq, _ = _stack()
    seq.save(td)
    for _ in range(steps):
        out, _ = seq.forward(Tensor(_SEG1))
        seq.backward(_total(out))
        seq.update(_LR)
        seq.save(td)
    return seq


def _chain_hash(td):
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    for name in sorted(os.listdir(td)):
        path = os.path.join(td, name)
        if os.path.isfile(path):
            digest.update(name.encode("ascii"))
            with open(path, "rb") as fh:
                digest.update(fh.read())
    return digest.hexdigest()


def _renumber_delta(path, new_number):
    with open(path, "rb") as fh:
        raw = fh.read()
    hlen = struct.unpack("<Q", raw[12:20])[0]
    header = json.loads(raw[20 : 20 + hlen])
    payload = raw[20 + hlen : raw.rfind(cp.DELTA_END_MAGIC)]
    header["n"] = new_number
    new_header = json.dumps(
        header, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True
    ).encode("utf-8")
    body = (
        raw[:8]
        + struct.pack("<I", cp.FORMAT_VERSION)
        + struct.pack("<Q", len(new_header))
        + new_header
        + payload
    )
    crc = zlib.crc32(body[20:])
    return body + cp.DELTA_END_MAGIC + struct.pack(
        "<QI", len(payload) // 9, crc
    )


class StreamingCompactionTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_state_and_segment_count_after_streaming_compaction(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
            seq = _trained_dir(td, 5)
            full = cp.build_bytes(cp.load_chain(td))
            cp.compact_chain(td, up_to=2)
            with open(os.path.join(td, "head"), "rb") as fh:
                head = int(fh.read())
            self.assertEqual(head, 3)
            self.assertEqual(
                sorted(f for f in os.listdir(td) if f.startswith("seg-")),
                [_seg(i) for i in range(4)],
            )
            self.assertEqual(cp.build_bytes(cp.load_chain(td)), full)
            cp.compact_chain(td)
            self.assertEqual(
                sorted(os.listdir(td)), ["head", _seg(0)]
            )
            self.assertEqual(cp.build_bytes(cp.load_chain(td)), full)

    def test_peak_disk_usage_within_old_chain_plus_one_basis(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
            steps, fold = 30, 10
            _trained_dir(td, steps)
            old_total = sum(
                os.path.getsize(os.path.join(td, name))
                for name in os.listdir(td)
                if name.startswith("seg-")
            )

def test_killed_compaction_before_marker_keeps_old_chain(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
            seq, _ = _trained_chain(td, steps=30)  # head == 30
            expected = _chain_bytes(td)
            head_before = _read_file(os.path.join(td, "head"))

            proc = multiprocessing.Process(
                target=_compact_worker, args=(td, 1)
            )
            proc.start()
            # Kill as soon as the staging area appears (before the marker
            # can be written, or at worst mid-roll-forward).
            saw_staging = self._kill_after(
                proc,
                lambda: any(
                    name.startswith(".seqc-") for name in os.listdir(td)
                ),
            )

            # The chain loads to one complete state -- either the old head
            # (killed before the marker) or the rolled-forward new head
            # (killed after it); both reassemble to the same document.
            self.assertEqual(_chain_bytes(td), expected)
            if saw_staging:
                head_after = _read_file(os.path.join(td, "head"))
                self.assertIn(head_after, (head_before, b"29"))
            # Recovery leaves no staging debris behind.
            self.assertFalse(
                any(
                    name.startswith((".seqc-", ".seqcompact"))
                    for name in os.listdir(td)
                )
            )

    def test_killed_compaction_after_marker_rolls_forward(self):
        for _ in range(3):
            with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
                seq, _ = _trained_chain(td, steps=30)
                expected = _chain_bytes(td)
                proc = multiprocessing.Process(
                    target=_compact_worker, args=(td, 1)
                )
                proc.start()
                saw_marker = self._kill_after(
                    proc,
                    lambda: os.path.exists(os.path.join(td, ".seqcompact")),
                )
                # Whether the kill landed after the marker or the worker
                # finished first, the chain is complete and loads to the
                # preserved state.
                self.assertEqual(_chain_bytes(td), expected)
                if saw_marker or proc.exitcode == 0:
                    # The roll-forward completed on recovery: head moved
                    # and the staging area is gone.
                    with open(os.path.join(td, "head"), "rb") as fh:
                        self.assertEqual(fh.read(), b"29")
                    self.assertFalse(
                        any(
                            name.startswith((".seqc-", ".seqcompact"))
                            for name in os.listdir(td)
                        )
                    )

    def test_compaction_marker_protocol_directly(self):
        # Deterministic, no timing: stage a compaction by hand, then let
        # the next open roll it forward.
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
            seq, _ = _trained_chain(td)
            expected = _chain_bytes(td)
            # Stage a full compaction manually: staged basis + marker,
            # no roll-forward yet.
            folded = cp.build_bytes(cp.load_chain(td))
            cp._atomic_write(td, cp._staged_name(0), folded)
            cp._atomic_write(td, cp._COMPACT_MARKER, b"0")
            # The next open recovers to exactly the new head.
            self.assertEqual(_chain_bytes(td), expected)
            self.assertEqual(sorted(os.listdir(td)), ["head", _seg_name(0)])
            # A staged file without a marker is simply dropped.
            cp._atomic_write(td, cp._staged_name(0), folded)
            self.assertEqual(_chain_bytes(td), expected)
            self.assertEqual(sorted(os.listdir(td)), ["head", _seg_name(0)])


def _writer_process(td, rounds):
    """A second process appending to the same chain directory."""
    from sequence_engine._selftest import _concurrency_model

    seq, _a, _b = _concurrency_model()
    seq.forward(Tensor([[1, 1]]))
    seq.backward(1)
    for _ in range(rounds):
        seq.update(1)
        seq.save(td)

# Family compaction commit protocol.  The fold common to every member is
# staged under this name inside each member directory (a per-directory
# file, so it is reclaimed by hard-link reachability together with the
# folded prefix) and a marker names the fold while publication runs.  The
# marker records the fold point ("u"), the post-fold head each member
# will adopt ("m": [..]), and the family-wide lease fd ("l") held for the
# whole run; it is written into every member directory, so any member
# opened after a kill rolls the fold forward (the flock fence makes
# exactly one opener win).

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Family compaction: folding a whole chain family's shared history once
#
# A family produced by forks keeps the same history in every member's
# prefix slots (the prefix files are hard links -- one physical copy).
# Family compaction folds the prefix *every* member's head reaches into
# one new basis segment:
#
#   1. every member is opened (any interrupted single-chain fold is
#      rolled forward and a live one waited out first), each chain is
#      validated through its head and its head state assembled;
#   2. the longest prefix whose segment bytes are identical across all
#      members (they are the same physical files) is the fold range;
#      nothing folds when that range is just the basis;
#   3. the folded basis is staged inside one member directory and hard
#      linked into the others, so the new basis is physically stored once
#      exactly as the old prefix was;
#   4. a marker naming the fold point and the post-fold heads is published
#      into every member directory (each under that member's directory
#      lock), together with one family-wide lease; only then do the
#      destructive member publications run -- folded prefix release,
#      basis promotion and tail rotation, exactly the resumable
#      publication of a single-chain fold;
#   5. each member's head advances to its own post-fold segment and its
#      marker is removed last.
#
# A kill at any point leaves every member's head naming one complete
# chain -- the old one or the new one.  Recovery is driven by the marker:
# an opener (a load, a save, a single-chain compact/fork/delete/merge)
# rolls the whole family forward, and an exclusive flock on the family
# lease fences openers so exactly one of them performs the roll while the
# others wait for it under their directory locks.  Folding is a pure
# function of the reachable segment bytes: the segment count drops
# deterministically by exactly the common folded range, repeating the
# same fold changes nothing (it then finds nothing to fold), and no
# member's optimizer step is advanced.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _family_staged_name():
    return _FAMILY_STAGED_PREFIX + _segment_name(_BASIS_INDEX)


def _family_marker_path(directory):
    return os.path.join(directory, _FAMILY_MARKER)


def _family_marker_exists(directory):
    return os.path.exists(_family_marker_path(directory))


def _encode_family_marker(marker):
    return json.dumps(marker, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")).encode(
        "ascii"
    )


def _decode_family_marker(raw):
    """Parse a family-compaction marker.

    ``{"u": fold, "m": [post-fold heads], "l": lease directory}`` -- the
    fold is in force in every member that carries it.  Decoding failures
    and structurally wrong markers are reported as corrupt.
    """
    try:
        marker = json.loads(raw.decode("ascii"))
    except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError):
        raise CheckpointError("family compaction marker is corrupt") from None
    if not isinstance(marker, dict) or set(marker) != {"u", "m", "l"}:
        raise CheckpointError("family compaction marker is corrupt")
    fold = marker["u"]
    if isinstance(fold, bool) or not isinstance(fold, int) or fold <= 0:
        raise CheckpointError("family compaction marker is corrupt")
    members = marker["m"]
    if not isinstance(members, list) or not members:
        raise CheckpointError("family compaction marker is corrupt")
    for head in members:
        if isinstance(head, bool) or not isinstance(head, int) or head < 0:
            raise CheckpointError("family compaction marker is corrupt")
    lease_dir = marker["l"]
    if not isinstance(lease_dir, str) or not lease_dir:
        raise CheckpointError("family compaction marker is corrupt")
    return marker


def _family_lease_path(lease_dir):
    return os.path.join(lease_dir, _FAMILY_LOCK_NAME)


def _read_family_marker(directory):
    """The parsed family marker in *directory*, or ``None`` when absent."""
    path = _family_marker_path(directory)
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        return None
    with open(path, "rb") as fh:
        return _decode_family_marker(fh.read())


def _family_marker_live(directory, marker):
    """Whether the flock named by *marker* is held by a live process.

    Mirrors :func:`_marker_live`: an unheld exclusive lock means the
    owner died and the fold must be rolled forward.  Platforms without
    ``fcntl`` only get in-process fencing via the directory locks.
    """
    if fcntl is None:
        return False
    path = _family_lease_path(marker["l"])
    try:
        fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDONLY)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        # The lease file is normally the last thing dropped from the
        # anchor directory.  Its absence while a marker still names it
        # means the publication reached the anchor cleanup: treat the
        # fold as dead so the opener finishes publishing the members.
        return False
    try:
        try:
            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
        except OSError as exc:
            if exc.errno in (errno.EWOULDBLOCK, errno.EAGAIN, errno.EACCES):
                return True
            return False
        try:
            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
        except OSError:
            pass
        return False
    finally:
        os.close(fd)


def _wait_family_lease(marker):
    """Block until the family fold's lease is free (owner finished/died)."""
    if fcntl is None:
        return
    path = _family_lease_path(marker["l"])
    try:
        fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDONLY)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return
    try:
        fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
        try:
            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
        except OSError:
            pass
    finally:
        os.close(fd)


def _acquire_family_lease(lease_dir):
    """Create the family lease file and take its exclusive flock.

    Returns the locked fd (an fd-less sentinel on platforms without
    ``fcntl``).  The lease is held for the whole fold and released by the
    kernel if the owner is killed.
    """
    fd = os.open(_family_lease_path(lease_dir), os.O.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT, 0o644)
    if fcntl is not None:
        fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
    return fd


def _release_family_lease(fd):
    if not fd:
        return
    try:
        if fcntl is not None:
            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
    except OSError:
        pass
    try:
        os.close(fd)
    except OSError:
        pass


def _same_family_file(paths, index):
    """Whether segment *index* is byte-identical across every directory.

    Identity by hard link (``os.path.samefile``) is the common case after
    a fork; a byte-for-byte comparison also accepts a prefix that was
    copied rather than linked, so sharing is detected by content rather
    than by how the family was built.
    """
    names = [os.path.join(path, _segment_name(index)) for path in paths]
    try:
        if all(os.path.samefile(names[0], name) for name in names[1:]):
            return True
    except OSError:
        pass
    try:
        with open(names[0], "rb") as fh:
            first = fh.read()
        for name in names[1:]:
            with open(name, "rb") as fh:
                if fh.read() != first:
                    return False
    except FileNotFoundError:
        raise
    except OSError:
        return False
    return True


def _open_family_member(directory):
    """Open one member quiescent: wait out live folds, roll dead ones.

    Returns ``(store, head)`` with no single-chain or family marker in
    the directory.  A family fold is waited out (never rolled) here:
    recovery happens at exactly one fenced point in
    :func:`_recover_directory_chain`, which owns this member's directory
    lock; this helper only services the wait loop of family operations.
    """
    while True:
        with _DirectoryChainLock(directory):
            store = _DirectoryChainStore(directory)
            _recover_directory_chain(directory, store)
            family = _read_family_marker(directory)
            if family is None and not _marker_exists(directory):
                head = _read_head_optional(store)
                if head is None:
                    raise CheckpointError(
                        "chain has no head pointer (no basis segment committed)"
                    )
                return store, head
        if family is not None:
            _wait_family_lease(family)
        else:
            _wait_for_live_marker(directory)


def compact_family(members):
    """Fold the common history prefix of a whole chain family into one
    new basis segment.

    *members* is a non-empty sequence of chain directories belonging to
    one family (the result of one or more forks).  The basis and the
    delta prefix every member's head reaches -- the segments physically
    shared after the forks -- are folded into one new basis segment
    written in the current format version.  Every member's ``head`` then
    names the folded chain: the common basis followed by the member's
    own, untouched tail deltas.  The new basis is stored once (hard
    linked across the member directories, exactly like the prefix it
    replaces) and the old prefix copies are released, so a shared
    segment keeps being stored once and is reclaimed by reachability
    exactly when no member can reach it.

    Each member's reassembled state -- parameters, gradients, optimizer
    moments and step count, hidden state -- is bit for bit identical
    before and after; the fold advances no member's optimizer step, and
    the semantics of both an unstepped chain (``t = 0``) and a stepped
    chain are preserved.  The segment count of every member drops by
    exactly the folded range; folding the same family again is a no-op
    (once folded, the common range is just the basis and nothing folds),
    as is a family with no foldable prefix.  Saves and loads proceed
    normally throughout and no member is ever observed as half a chain;
    a process killed midway leaves every member loadable as one complete
    state and the next family operation (or the next open of any member)
    deterministically rolls the fold forward and reclaims the residue,
    serialised against forks, merges, deletions and single-chain
    compactions by the directory locks and the family lease -- shared
    segments are neither deleted while reachable nor leaked.

    A missing member directory or a referenced segment that is absent
    raises ``FileNotFoundError`` without touching the other members.  A
    truncated segment, a missing field, an out-of-order segment, or
    members whose parameter shapes or layer order disagree rejects the
    whole fold with ``ValueError`` -- the message names the mismatching
    shapes and layer order -- before any member is changed by a byte.
    An unwritable directory or a full disk raises ``OSError``.
    """
    paths = _check_family_members(members)
    abs_paths = [os.path.abspath(path) for path in paths]
    if len(set(abs_paths)) != len(abs_paths):
        raise CheckpointError("a chain family cannot list the same member twice")
    for path in abs_paths:
        if not os.path.isdir(path):
            raise FileNotFoundError(
                f"incremental checkpoint directory not found: {path!r}"
            )
    # Deterministic GC of killed fork/delete staging in the family
    # directories' parents before the fold starts.
    parents = sorted({os.path.dirname(path) for path in abs_paths})
    for parent in parents:
        _sweep_parent_staging(parent)

    # Phase 1: open every member quiescent, validate the whole reachable
    # chain and capture the folded document -- all before one byte is
    # written.  A failure here rejects the fold with every member intact.
    opened = [_open_family_member(path) for path in abs_paths]
    heads = [head for _store, head in opened]
    stores = [store for store, _head in opened]
    fold_limit = min(heads)
    if fold_limit < 1:
        return None  # basis only everywhere: nothing to fold

    # The common prefix is decided by identical segment bytes, walking
    # from the basis.  Each read validates the segment exactly the way a
    # load does, so a defect is located at its segment and rejects the
    # whole family before staging begins.
    folded_doc = None
    fold = 0
    walkers = []
    for index, (store, head) in enumerate(zip(stores, heads)):
        walkers.append(_ChainWalker(store.read_segment(_segment_name(0))))
    for segment_index in range(1, fold_limit + 1):
        if not _same_family_file(abs_paths, segment_index):
            break
        raw = stores[0].read_segment(_segment_name(segment_index))
        for member_index, (walker, head) in enumerate(zip(walkers, heads)):
            # Every member reaches this segment (it is at or below the
            # smallest head) and its bytes are identical; the wire
            # number it carries is this position in every member.
            walker.apply_delta(segment_index, raw)
        fold = segment_index
    if fold == 0:
        return None  # no common delta prefix: nothing to fold
    folded_doc = walkers[0].document()

    # Every member must describe the same model -- parameter shapes and
    # layer order -- for one basis to serve all of them.  The shared
    # prefix already forces the shapes through *fold*; compare the head
    # documents explicitly so a tail that drifted is reported concretely.
    _check_family_compatibility(abs_paths, stores, heads, walkers)

    folded_bytes = build_bytes(folded_doc)
    post_heads = [head - fold for head in heads]
    lease_dir = abs_paths[0]

    # Phase 2: hold one family-wide lease for the whole publication, then
    # stage the folded basis (once on disk, hard-linked into every member
    # directory) and publish the marker into every member.  Each marker
    # write happens under that member's directory lock, so an opener can
    # never miss a fold that already released the member's prefix.
    lease_fd = _acquire_family_lease(lease_dir)
    try:
        staged_anchor = os.path.join(lease_dir, _family_staged_name())
        _atomic_write(lease_dir, _family_staged_name(), folded_bytes)
        marker_bytes = _encode_family_marker(
            {"u": fold, "m": post_heads, "l": lease_dir}
        )
        for path in abs_paths[1:]:
            if os.path.abspath(path) != lease_dir:
                target = os.path.join(path, _family_staged_name())
                if not os.path.exists(target):
                    os.link(staged_anchor, target)
        for path in abs_paths:
            with _DirectoryChainLock(path):
                _atomic_write(path, _FAMILY_MARKER, marker_bytes)
        _fsync_directory(lease_dir)

        # Phase 3: publish the members one at a time.  A kill between
        # members is recovered by the next open of any surviving member.
        for member_index, path in enumerate(abs_paths):
            _publish_family_member(
                path, fold, post_heads[member_index], lease_dir, final=False
            )
        # The last member is the lease anchor: once it publishes, the
        # lease and its staged file can finally go.
        _publish_family_member(
            lease_dir, fold, post_heads[0], lease_dir, final=True
        )
    except BaseException:
        # A live caller giving up (a full disk, say) releases the lease;
        # the next open of any member rolls the same deterministic steps
        # forward, fenced by the lease.
        _release_family_lease(lease_fd)
        raise
    _release_family_lease(lease_fd)
    return None


def _check_family_members(members):
    if isinstance(members, (str, bytes, os.PathLike)):
        raise TypeError("a chain family must be a sequence of chain directories")
    try:
        members = list(members)
    except TypeError:
        raise TypeError(
            "a chain family must be a sequence of chain directories"
        ) from None
    if not members:
        raise CheckpointError("a chain family needs at least one chain")
    paths = []
    for member in members:
        if not isinstance(member, (str, os.PathLike)):
            raise TypeError("chain family members must be chain directory paths")
        paths.append(os.fspath(member))
    return paths


def _layer_order_signature(document):
    return [
        (layer["kind"], [list(shape) for shape in layer["shapes"]])
        for layer in document["layers"]
    ]


def _check_family_compatibility(paths, stores, heads, prefix_walkers):
    """Assemble each head and demand identical model shapes/layer order.

    The shared prefix walkers already folded the common range; each
    member's own tail is applied on top and the full head document is
    compared.  A disagreement is rejected with the mismatching shapes
    and layer order written into the message.
    """
    head_documents = []
    for member_index, (store, head) in enumerate(zip(stores, heads)):
        walker = prefix_walkers[member_index]
        fold_limit = min(heads)
        for segment_index in range(fold_limit + 1, head + 1):
            walker.apply_delta(
                segment_index, store.read_segment(_segment_name(segment_index))
            )
        head_documents.append(walker.document())

    reference = head_documents[0]
    ref_param_shapes = [list(entry["s"]) for entry in reference["params"]]
    ref_layers = _layer_order_signature(reference)
    for member_index, document in enumerate(head_documents[1:], start=1):
        param_shapes = [list(entry["s"]) for entry in document["params"]]
        if param_shapes != ref_param_shapes:
            raise CheckpointError(
                "family compaction rejected: chain "
                f"{member_index} ({paths[member_index]!r}) parameter shapes "
                f"{param_shapes!r} do not match chain 0 ({paths[0]!r}) "
                f"parameter shapes {ref_param_shapes!r}"
            )
        layers = _layer_order_signature(document)
        if layers != ref_layers:
            raise CheckpointError(
                "family compaction rejected: chain "
                f"{member_index} ({paths[member_index]!r}) layer order "
                f"{layers!r} does not match chain 0 ({paths[0]!r}) layer "
                f"order {ref_layers!r}"
            )


def _publish_family_member(directory, fold, new_head, lease_dir, final):
    """Publish one member: same resumable steps as a single-chain fold.

    The member's directory lock is held for the rotation, so an append or
    a load observes either the old head chain or the new one.  The marker
    stays until every member is published; on the final (anchor) member
    the staged basis, the family markers and the lease are reclaimed.
    """
    with _DirectoryChainLock(directory):
        store = _DirectoryChainStore(directory)
        staged_path = os.path.join(directory, _family_staged_name())
        with open(staged_path, "rb") as fh:
            staged_basis = fh.read()
        _atomic_write(directory, _segment_name(_BASIS_INDEX), staged_basis)
        for index in range(1, fold + 1):
            _unlink_quietly(os.path.join(directory, _segment_name(index)))
        _promote_tail_slots(directory, fold, new_head)
        for name in list(os.listdir(directory)):
            index = _segment_index(name)
            if index is not None and index > new_head:
                _unlink_quietly(os.path.join(directory, name))
        _commit_head(store, new_head)
        _unlink_quietly(staged_path)
        _unlink_quietly(_family_marker_path(directory))
        _fsync_directory(directory)
        if final:
            # Every member is published.  Other members' staged files
            # were hard links to this one physical file; their unlinks
            # already happened, so this is the last reference.
            for path in _family_marker_dirs(lease_dir, directory):
                pass
            _unlink_quietly(_family_lease_path(lease_dir))
            _fsync_directory(lease_dir)


def _family_marker_dirs(lease_dir, directory):
    return ()


def _roll_forward_family_fold(directory, marker):
    """Finish an interrupted family fold for every member, fenced.

    Called from :func:`_recover_directory_chain` under *directory*'s
    directory lock.  An exclusive flock on the family lease makes exactly
    one opener the finisher; it publishes each member that still carries
    the marker, waiting on each member's directory lock in turn.  Other
    openers block on the lease and then simply re-open their member.
    """
    lease_dir = marker["l"]
    fold = marker["u"]
    post_heads = marker["m"]
    fd = None
    if fcntl is not None:
        try:
            lease_fd = os.open(_family_lease_path(lease_dir), os.O_RDWR)
        except FileNotFoundError:
            lease_fd = None
        if lease_fd is not None:
            fcntl.flock(lease_fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
            fd = lease_fd
    try:
        members = _family_member_dirs(directory, marker)
        for member_index, path in enumerate(members):
            if not os.path.isdir(path):
                # A member deleted while the fold was dead cannot be
                # recovered; its segment references were already
                # released and the remaining members finish on their own.
                continue
            if not _family_marker_exists(path):
                continue
            with _DirectoryChainLock(path):
                member_store = _DirectoryChainStore(path)
                member_head = _read_head_optional(member_store)
                if member_head is None:
                    continue
                if member_head == post_heads[member_index] and not os.path.exists(
                    os.path.join(path, _family_staged_name())
                ):
                    # Already published: only debris may remain.
                    _finish_family_member_cleanup(
                        path, fold, post_heads[member_index]
                    )
                    continue
                _finish_family_member(
                    path, fold, post_heads[member_index], lease_dir,
                    is_anchor=(os.path.abspath(path) == os.path.abspath(lease_dir)),
                )
    finally:
        if fd is not None:
            try:
                fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
            except OSError:
                pass
            os.close(fd)


def _family_member_dirs(opener_directory, marker):
    """Locate the family members carrying this fold.

    The marker does not record paths (they may have been renamed aside by
    a delete); members are found as the sibling chain directories that
    carry an identical family marker, plus the opener itself and the
    lease anchor.  Read-only best effort: directories that cannot be
    read are skipped here and recovered from their own next open.
    """
    opener_abs = os.path.abspath(opener_directory)
    lease_abs = os.path.abspath(marker["l"])
    candidates = [opener_abs]
    for base in sorted({os.path.dirname(opener_abs), os.path.dirname(lease_abs)}):
        try:
            names = os.listdir(base)
        except OSError:
            continue
        for name in names:
            path = os.path.join(base, name)
            if not os.path.isdir(path):
                continue
            abs_path = os.path.abspath(path)
            if abs_path in candidates or abs_path == lease_abs and lease_abs in candidates:
                continue
            marker_path = _family_marker_path(path)
            if not os.path.exists(marker_path):
                continue
            try:
                with open(marker_path, "rb") as fh:
                    other = _decode_family_marker(fh.read())
            except (CheckpointError, OSError):
                continue
            if other == marker:
                candidates.append(abs_path)
    if lease_abs not in candidates:
        candidates.append(lease_abs)
    # Order members as the marker does: the lease anchor carries
    # post-head 0; the opener (when not the anchor) is wherever it sits.
    # The marker's head list is positional, so recover a stable ordering
    # anchored on the lease directory first.
    ordered = [lease_abs] + [p for p in candidates if p != lease_abs]
    return ordered


def _finish_family_member(directory, fold, new_head, lease_dir, is_anchor):
    """Complete one member's publication during recovery."""
    store = _DirectoryChainStore(directory)
    staged_path = os.path.join(directory, _family_staged_name())
    if os.path.exists(staged_path):
        with open(staged_path, "rb") as fh:
            staged_basis = fh.read()
        _atomic_write(directory, _segment_name(_BASIS_INDEX), staged_basis)
    for index in range(1, fold + 1):
        _unlink_quietly(os.path.join(directory, _segment_name(index)))
    _promote_tail_slots(directory, fold, new_head)
    for name in list(os.listdir(directory)):
        index = _segment_index(name)
        if index is not None and index > new_head:
            _unlink_quietly(os.path.join(directory, name))
    _commit_head(store, new_head)
    _unlink_quietly(staged_path)
    _unlink_quietly(_family_marker_path(directory))
    _fsync_directory(directory)
    if is_anchor:
        _unlink_quietly(_family_lease_path(lease_dir))
        _fsync_directory(lease_dir)


def _finish_family_member_cleanup(directory, fold, new_head):
    """Drop residue from a member whose head already switched."""
    _promote_tail_slots(directory, fold, new_head)
    for name in list(os.listdir(directory)):
        index = _segment_index(name)
        if name.startswith(_FAMILY_STAGED_PREFIX) or (
            index is not None and index > new_head
        ):
            _unlink_quietly(os.path.join(directory, name))
    _unlink_quietly(_family_marker_path(directory))
    _fsync_directory(directory)


def compact_family_memory(members):
    """Fold a family of in-memory chains; same semantics as
    :func:`compact_family`.

    The common prefix is shared by object identity (forked memory chains
    reference the same segment bytes); one folded basis object is placed
    in every member and each member's own tail follows it.  The whole
    fold runs under the member locks, so it is one critical section with
    identical results.
    """
    if isinstance(members, MemoryChain):
        raise TypeError("a chain family must be a sequence of MemoryChains")
    try:
        members = list(members)
    except TypeError:
        raise TypeError(
            "a chain family must be a sequence of MemoryChains"
        ) from None
    if not members:
        raise CheckpointError("a chain family needs at least one chain")
    for member in members:
        if not isinstance(member, MemoryChain):
            raise TypeError("chain family members must be MemoryChains")
    if len(set(id(member) for member in members)) != len(members):
        raise CheckpointError("a chain family cannot list the same member twice")
    locks = [member._lock for member in members]
    for lock in locks:
        lock.acquire()
    try:
        heads = []
        for member in members:
            head = _read_head_optional(member)
            if head is None:
                raise CheckpointError(
                    "chain has no head pointer (no basis segment committed)"
                )
            heads.append(head)
        fold_limit = min(heads)
        walkers = [
            _ChainWalker(member.read_segment(_segment_name(0))) for member in members
        ]
        fold = 0
        prefix_bytes = None
        for segment_index in range(1, fold_limit + 1):
            name = _segment_name(segment_index)
            raw = members[0].read_segment(name)
            if any(member.read_segment(name) is not raw for member in members[1:]):
                break
            for walker in walkers:
                walker.apply_delta(segment_index, raw)
            fold = segment_index
        if fold == 0:
            return None
        folded_doc = walkers[0].document()
        # Validate each head (the member's own tail included) and compare
        # model shapes and layer order before anything is replaced.
        documents = []
        for member, walker, head in zip(members, walkers, heads):
            for segment_index in range(fold + 1, head + 1):
                walker.apply_delta(
                    segment_index,
                    member.read_segment(_segment_name(segment_index)),
                )
            documents.append(walker.document())
        ref_shapes = [list(entry["s"]) for entry in documents[0]["params"]]
        ref_layers = _layer_order_signature(documents[0])
        for member_index, document in enumerate(documents[1:], start=1):
            shapes = [list(entry["s"]) for entry in document["params"]]
            if shapes != ref_shapes:
                raise CheckpointError(
                    "family compaction rejected: member "
                    f"{member_index} parameter shapes {shapes!r} do not match "
                    f"member 0 parameter shapes {ref_shapes!r}"
                )
            layers = _layer_order_signature(document)
            if layers != ref_layers:
                raise CheckpointError(
                    "family compaction rejected: member "
                    f"{member_index} layer order {layers!r} does not match "
                    f"member 0 layer order {ref_layers!r}"
                )

        folded_bytes = build_bytes(folded_doc)
        new_tails = []
        for member, head in zip(members, heads):
            tail = {}
            for old_index in range(fold + 1, head + 1):
                tail[old_index - fold] = member.read_segment(
                    _segment_name(old_index)
                )
            new_tails.append(tail)
        post_heads = [head - fold for head in heads]
        for member, new_head, tail in zip(members, post_heads, new_tails):
            member.write_segment(_segment_name(0), folded_bytes)
            for new_index, raw in tail.items():
                member.write_segment(_segment_name(new_index), raw)
            for name in list(member._objects):
                index = _segment_index(name)
                if index is not None and index > new_head:
                    del member._objects[name]
            _commit_head(member, new_head)
    finally:
        for lock in reversed(locks):
            lock.release()
    return None

# Full / chain dispatch and file / memory IO
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
